title: AI Use-Case Evaluation in ERP and CRM Systems (2026)

questions.question: What system-boundary result does classify_system_boundary return for a use case spanning three platforms?
options: GREEN, because three systems provide more context for the model
AMBER, because any multi-platform use case needs only an integration note
RED, because three or more platforms require architecture sign-off
The function returns no result until data ownership is confirmed
questions.explanation: The classifier treats one platform as GREEN, two as AMBER, and three or more as RED. The multi-team integration surface must be reduced or explicitly signed off architecturally.

questions.question: What system_boundary RAG does the SalesforceCore plus SalesforceDataCloud use case receive?
options: GREEN, because both names belong to Salesforce
RED, because every cross-system read is autonomous
GREEN, because read_recommend never crosses a boundary
AMBER, because two platforms require an integration contract
questions.explanation: classify_system_boundary uses the platform count first: any two platforms are AMBER. The read/recommend pattern affects a separate axis and does not erase the integration contract.

questions.question: Why is the Agentforce autonomous case-routing sample BLOCKED?
options: It has RED integration and compliance axes: three platforms, PII, and no confirmed residency
It is READY because autonomous_bounded is a green integration pattern
It is only CONDITIONAL because PII always produces an amber result when an owner exists
It is BLOCKED solely because the use case reads from Salesforce
questions.explanation: The sample has three platforms and an open autonomous pattern, both producing RED axes; PII without confirmed residency also produces RED compliance. Any red axis makes evaluate return BLOCKED.

questions.question: What readiness does the Dynamics 365 plus S4HANA financial read-summarize use case receive?
options: READY, because read_summarize is green on every axis
CONDITIONAL, because the two-platform boundary and sensitive financial data are amber
BLOCKED, because two vendors are always a red boundary
CONDITIONAL only if data ownership is unconfirmed
questions.explanation: Two cross-vendor platforms are AMBER, and confirmed sensitive financial data is also AMBER. Ownership and residency pass, so there is no RED axis and the overall result is CONDITIONAL.

questions.question: What happens when data_owner_confirmed=False for an otherwise single-platform use case?
options: The axis stays GREEN because platform scope determines ownership
The result becomes CONDITIONAL only when the integration writes data
The data_ownership axis becomes RED and evaluate returns BLOCKED
The owner check is skipped for operational data
questions.explanation: The data-ownership classifier returns RED whenever no owner is confirmed. A single RED axis is enough for evaluate to mark the use case BLOCKED, regardless of platform count.

questions.question: Why must the evaluator be run again if a discovery-stage read_summarize design becomes autonomous_open?
options: The model vendor changes automatically whenever integration changes
Read_summarize and autonomous_open have identical risk, so the rerun is only for logging
The evaluation cache cannot store more than one pattern per use case
The integration-pattern axis can move from GREEN to RED, so the earlier readiness result is no longer valid
questions.explanation: read-only summarization is GREEN on the integration axis, while autonomous_open is RED. The lesson therefore requires re-evaluation rather than inheriting a discovery-stage approval.
